clue.text: Negotiators faced with ruin — they're shaken

indicators.note: the negotiators have ruin set before them, so that word comes first

parts.note: to ruin is to mar
ACAS is the UK's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which negotiates in industrial disputes

explanation.surface: Industrial mediators confront collapse and are badly rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British body that brokers settlements between employers and unions; 'they're shaken' looks like a description of the rattled negotiators.
explanation.definitionFit: These percussion instruments are gourds filled with beads that sound when shaken.

clue.text: Vehicle doctor keeps at home, one vehicle not right

indicators.note: keeps says the doctor holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: not right says R, short for right, is removed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps a car at home, one with a faulty right side.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a taxi booked by phone, a vehicle for hire.

clue.text: Toy, not the first to be put in sack

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to trifle with is to toy with

explanation.surface: A plaything, not the top one, is to be stuffed into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag, but here it is the verb meaning plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack or plunder it.

clue.text: Keen to have gym in the basement

indicators.note: to have says the cry is followed by the gym

parts.note: to keen is to wail, cry
PT is physical training, gym lessons

explanation.surface: Eager to have a workout room downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the verb meaning wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber, a basement beneath a church.

clue.text: Matrimonial lapsus unfortunately stifles love

indicators.note: stifles says the jumble smothers the next piece inside it
unfortunately says the letters of lapsus are badly arranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A marital slip of the tongue sadly kills off affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' makes SPUSAL from LAPSUS, with O placed inside; a lapsus is a slip or lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Spousal means relating to a spouse, so to marriage.

clue.text: Like a racehorse last in The Oaks — rotten!

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the race's name that follows

parts.note: an addled egg is rotten

explanation.surface: A horse finishing last in the famous Epsom race is lamented as dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a classic flat race run at Epsom in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse wears a saddle for its jockey, so it is described as saddled up.

clue.text: Hull, with English poetry's ultimate poet

parts.note: a hull is a shell or husk

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter of poetry's

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire city's English verse produces a great poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the city in northern England; it means a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Travel a great distance, covering a hundred and one homes

parts.note: to do a distance is to travel it

indicators.note: covering says the travelling phrase surrounds the numbers

parts.note: miles means a long way
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Journey far to visit a hundred and one houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a place of residence, a home.

clue.text: Like some weather forecasts, look — no good when going over mountains!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means sitting above the mountains

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: Forecasters warn the outlook is poor once you cross the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range forecasts predict weather far ahead.

clue.text: Pick out various bits from cinders

indicators.note: various bits from says the letters of cinders are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sift through the remains of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to detect or make out, so to pick out.

clue.text: Exclusion area — in which spiders have been 100% efficient?

definitions.text: in which spiders have been 100% efficient?
definitions.meaning: a place where spiders have caught every insect, so not one fly remains

explanation.surface: A forbidden airspace is joked about as a place cleared by perfect spiders.
explanation.definitionFit: This is airspace barred to aircraft, an exclusion area; read literally it is a place without a single fly.

clue.text: Lists of American soldiers at the front

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed in front of the American

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Rosters of American troops serving on the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Menus are lists of dishes, or of options on a computer screen.

clue.text: Makes boxes for drug containment

indicators.note: containment says the boxes hold the drug inside them

parts.note: crates are boxes
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A company produces boxes designed to hold narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To create something is to make it, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Superior research establishment in the French part of Switzerland

indicators.note: in says the first two pieces sit inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior
CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A top laboratory located in the French-speaking region of Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests CERN itself, which is near Geneva; the answer is a Swiss city and canton.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a city and canton in central Switzerland.

clue.text: Singer's corny stuff enthralling silly mob

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the grain surrounds the jumble

parts.note: barley is a cereal grain, corn in the British sense

indicators.note: silly says the letters of mob are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer's cheesy material captivates a foolish crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests trite, but here it means made of corn, a grain; 'silly' signals the anagram of the crowd word, held inside by 'enthralling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was the Jamaican reggae singer and songwriter.

clue.text: Bitchy sort of person, but not an incisive type

definitions.meaning: someone who speaks spitefully about people behind their backs
a tooth at the back, a molar, rather than an incisor at the front

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip, though not a sharp one.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbiter slanders absent people; read literally it is a back tooth, not a front incisor.

clue.text: Anatolia is confused with Romania

indicators.note: confused says the letters of is and Romania are mixed up

explanation.surface: Turkey's ancient peninsula gets mixed up with a Balkan country.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the historical name for Anatolia, the Asian part of Turkey.

clue.text: Wrinkle on new material

parts.note: a wrinkle is a line on the skin

explanation.surface: A crease appears on freshly bought fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a cloth woven from flax, a material.

clue.text: Plants contributing to atmospheric activity

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Greenery said to play a part in weather and climate processes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulent plants of dry regions.

clue.text: Stops talking about bashes at Oxford?

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to lam is to beat, bash
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Falls silent about the parties held at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bashes' looks like parties, but is the verb for thrashes; being UP means in residence at a university like Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is to refuse to talk, an idiom.

clue.text: London area's leader embraces a politician, good man?

indicators.note: embraces says the leader's letters wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: a head is a leader
MP is a Member of Parliament
ST stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: The head of a London district hugs a member of parliament, a decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPSTEAD is a well-off district of north London; 'area's leader' reads as a local boss, but the 's is 'is' and HEAD alone is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead is a district of north London, known for its heath.

clue.text: A plant in truth!

definitions.meaning: a flowering plant with flat silvery seed pods, Lunaria

explanation.surface: A plant hidden in the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is both truthfulness and a garden plant with silvery pods.

clue.text: Wise men having no time for one wanting to hold the line

definitions.text: one wanting to hold the line

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wise men lack time for someone trying to defend a border.
explanation.walkthrough: André Maginot was the French minister behind the fortified Maginot Line against Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Maginot gave his name to the French defensive line, so he wanted to hold that line.

clue.text: Part of the diocese yearned for change

indicators.note: for change says the letters of yearned are reordered

explanation.surface: A section of the church district longed for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A deanery is a group of parishes under a rural dean, part of a diocese.

clue.text: Protein book now available at the bookshop?

parts.note: an album is a book of photos or stamps
a book that is in stock is 'in'

explanation.surface: A protein textbook has just arrived in the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumin is a water-soluble protein found in egg white and blood.

clue.text: Member of family would make splendid secretary

parts.note: grand means splendid
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A relative would be an excellent office assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a member of the family, informally called by this name.

clue.text: Respecting neighbour possessing nothing

indicators.note: possessing says the bordering word holds the zero inside

parts.note: to abut is to neighbour, border on
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The man next door owns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' looks like a noun but is the verb, to border.
explanation.definitionFit: About means concerning or regarding, so respecting.

clue.text: Stupid person beginning to cry is buried in sand

indicators.note: is buried in says that letter goes inside the sand hill

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of cry

explanation.surface: A fool starts to weep and is buried in sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow learner, a stupid person.

clue.text: Attack taking minutes, moving west

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving west means read from right to left

parts.note: minutes of a meeting are notes

explanation.surface: An assault takes some time and heads westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' looks like time, but means a meeting's written record.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to attack them, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ray may be sought in this room

definitions.text: Ray may be sought in this room

parts.words: Ray may be sought in this room
parts.note: Ray looks like a man's name, but it is a ray of light from the sky's star, which people seek in a glazed room

explanation.surface: A man called Ray may be looked for in this room.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed room designed to catch the sunshine is where people seek its rays.

clue.text: After drink artist has little yen for paint

indicators.note: after says the artist and the rest follow the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: little means only a small part, the first letter, of the word yen

explanation.surface: After a drink an artist has no great urge to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like a longing; here only its first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to paint or depict them.

clue.text: Unstable baby with aim to get round edge of table

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: to get round says the attempt wraps the letter that follows

parts.note: to try is to aim or attempt

indicators.note: edge of picks the final letter of the word table

explanation.surface: A wobbly toddler tries to get round the corner of a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge of table' gives its last letter E, which goes inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means shaky or unsteady on the feet, so unstable.
